title: Development of Therapeutic Target Discovery Strategies for Age-Related Diseases Aggravated by Senescence-Associated Immune Cells - Metabolic Dysregulation in Senescence-Associated Immune Cells Revealed by ADGRG1 Reporter Mice-
content: Aging promotes thymic involution and leads to the accumulation of senescence-associated (SA) immune cells, which contribute to chronic inflammation, autoimmune diseases, and metabolic dysfunction. Recent research has revealed that pathogenic SA follicular helper T (SA-Tfh) cells, which express PD-1, and SA-B cells are key mediators of age-related immune disorders. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic adaptation mechanisms are involved in the long-term survival of these cells. In this review, we highlight findings from transcriptome and integrated bioinformatic analyses identifying ADGRG1 as a common feature across multiple PD-1-positive immune cell populations. We suggest that this marker may be linked to cellular stress resistance, longevity, and metabolic pathways involving coenzyme Q. Furthermore, we propose that dysregulated Caveolin-1 signaling may contribute to the breakdown of immune tolerance in pathogenic SA-B cells. Based on these insights, we argue that metabolic reprogramming is a defining characteristic of pathogenic SA immune cells and that pathways associated with ADGRG1 could serve as therapeutic targets. By targeting the metabolic networks that govern cellular fitness and immune tolerance, it may be possible to selectively eliminate or reprogram pathogenic SA immune cells, while preserving the host’s protective immune defenses during the aging process.
